title: The Gospel and Salvation
summary: A study of the apostolic gospel, God's gracious rescue through Christ, and the good works that follow rather than purchase salvation.

observations.text: Jesus announces the kingdom of God and calls hearers to repent and believe the gospel.
Paul summarizes the received gospel around Christ's death for sins, burial, resurrection, and appearances to witnesses.
Ephesians describes people as spiritually dead and following sinful desires before emphasizing God's mercy, love, and action in making them alive with Christ.
The passage excludes boasting in human works while also saying believers are created in Christ for good works prepared by God.

teaching.text: The gospel calls for repentance and faith rather than mere assent or religious performance.
The Christian gospel centers on the real death and resurrection of Jesus Christ for sinners, not merely on moral improvement.
Salvation is God's gracious gift received through faith, leaving no basis for self-congratulation before God.
Good works are the intended fruit and path of the saved life, not the price paid to obtain God's grace.

interpretive_cautions.text: The gospel should not be reduced to reciting a formula or recalling an emotional moment while ignoring enduring trust in the crucified and risen Christ.

Faithful evangelical traditions differ over election, the extent of the atonement, perseverance, baptism's relation to conversion, and the order of salvation; these passages establish the gospel's center without resolving every part of those debates.

application: Turn from sin and trust the crucified and risen Christ rather than personal merit or religious performance.
Receive grace with humility and abandon boasting over other people.
Practice the good works God gives you to do as the fruit of new life, not as leverage over God.
discussion: Which parts of Paul's gospel summary are essential rather than optional?
How does grace confront both despair and pride?
What good work could flow from gratitude for salvation this week?
prayer: Merciful God, keep our confidence in Jesus Christ, who died and rose. Free us from boasting, teach us to receive grace, and shape our lives into grateful service.
